propositions: BindingStore's 799-line module conflates byte persistence, lifecycle policy, retirement, recovery, and peer-state delegation with no cohesive owner or safety rules enforcement.

Production code mutates inner entries returned by shallow all_bindings() query, creating regression risk for crash handling, index lag, identity management, serialization, and selective publication behavior.

Durable tombstone retirement completion requires agreement between tombstone, forward binding, and reverse binding identities; only explicit unretire revokes intent and automatic liveness never resurrects tombstoned identity.
Recovery must execute after staleness validation but before remote issue fetch and binding walk to prevent interleaving new liveness evidence with completion of interrupted retirements.

Extract three internal owners (repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, recovery) behind unchanged BindingStore facade while preserving all_bindings() shallow compatibility, unknown-field handling, byte-exact serialization, and five-file selective publication.
